residencyRequirements.description: The petition is filed where the marriage was solemnized, or where the parties last resided together, or where the respondent resides, or where the petitioner resides (at the time of filing when the wife is the petitioner). See HMA s.19 / SMA s.31.

waitingPeriod.description: Mutual consent: 6-month cooling-off period between First Motion and Second Motion (HMA s.13B(2) / SMA s.28(2)). Courts may waive this per Amardeep Singh v. Harveen Kaur (2017) 8 SCC 746. SC may also grant divorce under Art. 142 on irretrievable breakdown (Shilpa Sailesh v. Varun Sreenivasan (2023)). Contested: no fixed waiting period.

noFault.name: Mutual Consent
noFault.description: Both spouses jointly petition after living separately for at least one year. 6-month cooling-off period applies (may be waived).

noFault.name: No Resumption of Cohabitation after Judicial Separation
noFault.description: No resumption of cohabitation for one year or upwards after a decree for judicial separation (either party may petition).

noFault.name: No Restitution of Conjugal Rights after Decree
noFault.description: No restitution of conjugal rights for one year or upwards after a decree for restitution of conjugal rights (either party may petition).

fault.name: Adultery
fault.description: Voluntary sexual intercourse with a person other than the petitioner after solemnization.

fault.name: Cruelty
fault.description: Physical or mental cruelty by spouse.

fault.name: Desertion
fault.description: Desertion for a continuous period of not less than two years.

fault.name: Conversion
fault.description: Spouse has converted to another religion (HMA only).

fault.name: Unsoundness of Mind
fault.description: Incurably of unsound mind or suffering from mental disorder.

fault.name: Venereal Disease
fault.description: Suffering from venereal disease in communicable form.

fault.name: Presumed Dead
fault.description: Not heard of as alive for 7+ years.

wifeAdditional.name: Pre-Act Bigamy (wife only)
wifeAdditional.description: The husband had another wife living at the time of the marriage (applies only to marriages solemnized before the Hindu Marriage Act commenced on 18 May 1955).

wifeAdditional.name: Rape, Sodomy, or Bestiality by Husband (wife only)
wifeAdditional.description: The husband has been guilty of rape, sodomy, or bestiality since the solemnization of the marriage.

wifeAdditional.name: Maintenance Decree with No Cohabitation (wife only)
wifeAdditional.description: A maintenance decree or order (Hindu Adoptions and Maintenance Act 1956 s.18, or CrPC s.125 — now BNSS s.144) has been passed against the husband, and cohabitation has not been resumed for one year or upwards since.

wifeAdditional.name: Option of Puberty (wife only)
wifeAdditional.description: Her marriage (whether consummated or not) was solemnized before she attained fifteen years and she repudiated it after attaining that age but before attaining eighteen years.

terminology.maritalProperty: No specific matrimonial property regime; Hindu Succession Act 1956 / court-ordered settlement

basic.name: Petition for Divorce
basic.description: Filed under applicable personal law with affidavit on stamp paper

basic.name: Affidavit of the Petitioner
basic.description: Sworn affidavit. Affidavits made for the immediate purpose of being filed in court are exempt from stamp duty (Maharashtra Stamp Act, Sch. I, Art. 4, exemption); standalone affidavits are executed on non-judicial stamp paper (Art. 4 duty INR 500 since the October 2024 amendment)

basic.name: Address Proof
basic.description: Aadhaar card, voter ID, passport, or utility bill

legalCitations.description: Marriage and divorce for Hindus, Buddhists, Jains, Sikhs

filingFees.notes: Filing fee varies by court. Indigent persons may apply for fee waiver.

childSupportGuidelines.guidelines: No statutory formula; court considers income, needs, and lifestyle
childSupportGuidelines.notes: BNSS s.144 (CrPC s.125) provides for maintenance

spousalSupportGuidelines.guidelines: HMA s.25 / s.24; SMA s.36-37; BNSS s.144
spousalSupportGuidelines.notes: No fixed formula; court considers duration, earning capacity, standard of living

effectiveDateRule: The decree takes effect from the date it is passed.
certificateNote: A certified copy of the decree may be obtained from the court registry.
